messages:
incidents-bot: Pager: high-severity - GPU pool saturation in aws-af-south-1. Autoscaler failing to provision additional nodes; queue length growing on inference-router (>1200 requests). Origin: capacity_exhaustion. Triggered at 2026-03-15T09:22:47Z.

alex: ack. I'm oncall. looking.

ops: i'm seeing heavy Pending pods and scale up stuck at the cloud provider step. kubernetes shows HPA at 450% target but cloud APIs returning quota errors.

alex: paste the error snippet from autoscaler logs?

ops: ```
Mar 15 09:23:05 autoscaler controller.go:321] scale-up failed: provider error: RequestLimitExceeded: You have reached the maximum number of GPUs for this account in af-south-1
status code: 400, request id: abc-123
```

maria: tagging @support.eng and @tara — potential customer impact: several customers in EMEA/AF region report timeouts and 429s for generation. We should prepare comms if failing over will cause slight latency bump.

support.eng: noted. current error rate for hosted-api route `/v1/generate` in af-south-1 is 18% errors over last 5m, median p95 latency increased from 120ms -> 900ms. Affected customers: finance-ml (prod), chatterly (ingestion jobs).

alex: mitigation plan ideas: 1) temporarily throttle batch sizes and reduce concurrency per host 2) reroute new requests from af-south-1 to eu-west-1 as soft-failover 3) enable smaller-quantized variant for non-SLA traffic to reduce GPU footprint. Which one do we do now?

ops: immediate: reduce `max_inflight_per_instance` from 64 -> 8 and set `batch.max_tokens` 2048 -> 1024. Commands:
```
curl -X POST https://runtime.internal/configs -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","max_inflight_per_instance":8,"batch.max_tokens":1024}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN'
```

alex: doing that now. applying config.

incidents-bot: Config apply succeeded (hash: a1b2c3). Observing queue.

ops: autoscaler cloud call still returning quota error. I opened AWS account support case (case id: 555-aws-afs-2026). Requested temporary GPU quota bump + explanation of priority for production. ETA from AWS: unknown, flagged as urgent.

maria: starting customer comms draft: "We've detected capacity constraints in the af-south-1 region causing elevated errors for some requests. We're actively rerouting traffic and reducing load to mitigate impact. We'll update within 30 minutes." Ping @support.eng for list of impacted accounts and SLAs.

support.eng: sending list. Shortlist: finance-ml (SLA: 99.95), chatterly (SLA: best-effort), dataflow-x (SLA: 99.9). finance-ml has 12 failing requests/min over the last 10m.

alex: let's start soft-failover to eu-west-1 for non-SLA or low-priority traffic. Keep finance-ml on fallback path only if they opt-in; coordinate with product. Ops, can you add rule to smart-router to prefer eu-west if origin region reports >15% errors?

ops: adding routing rule now. Patch: 
```
PATCH /internal/routing
{"policy":"prefer-region","when.error_rate.gt":15,"fallback":"eu-west-1"}
```

ops: applied. watch logs.

incidents-bot: Routing policy change deployed.

alex: monitoring... queue length started to drop from 1200 -> 480 over 2m. p95 latency for routed requests to eu-west-1 is ~220ms. Good.

maria: customer comms sent to finance-ml and chatterly: initial notification + ask if they want data export of failed requests. finance-ml replied: please route to eu-west and notify once resolved.

support.eng: noted. Will escalate finance-ml's case internally.

ops: additional mitigation: spin up lower-capacity fallback instances using `gpt-compat-8bit` variant on any remaining spare CPU-backed nodes to keep throughput for best-effort traffic. Command: 
```
run-deploy --model gpt-compat-8bit --replicas 6 --region af-south-1 --node-type cpu-fallback
```

alex: approved. deploy started.

ops: deploy finished. It handled ~15% of remaining queue. Combined with routing rule and reduced inflight, error rate dropped to 3.2% in af-south-1.

maria: good progress. timeline: incident declared at 09:22Z, major mitigations applied by 09:29Z. Need to handoff to next oncall for monitoring until AWS quota increase or longer-term remediation.

alex: I'm going to hand off to @tara (night oncall) in 20 minutes. Tara, you're IC for follow-ups: keep routing rule, watch for AWS case updates, coordinate with infra for a permanent quota increase, and prepare rollback plan for routing change.

tara: ack. I'll take it. I'll also prepare a small post-incident note and update the incident tracker with timeline and actions.

incidents-bot: Incident status -> mitigated (partial). Root cause: account-level GPU quota exhausted in aws-af-south-1; autoscaler unable to provision new GPU instances. Current state: routing + smaller-model fallback active, error rate reduced to acceptable threshold, AWS support case open.

alex: quick followups for postmortem: 1) add autoscaler pre-checks to detect quota limits earlier 2) implement cross-region pre-warm based on traffic patterns 3) add dynamic batch throttling rule as automated runbook 4) review account quota forecasting.

maria: I'll own customer follow-up and final comms. ops, open a postmortem doc and invite eng-runtime, infra, and support.

ops: created doc: https://internal.redwood/pmo/INC-3951234567. Invites sent.

support.eng: closing loop with finance-ml: they've accepted eu-west failover and saw reduced errors. will follow up with an incident summary and logs export.

tara: handing notes: keep AWS case id 555-aws-afs-2026 pinned. If no quota bump within 8 hours, start scheduled traffic migration for affected customers.

incidents-bot: Thread closed by alex at 2026-03-15T09:43:19Z (temporary mitigations in place).
